harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as router between lan-a (192.168.10.0/24, node2) and lan-b (192.168.20.0/24, node3) using previously-unassigned vtnet1/vtnet2 as opt1/opt2. Added firewall pass rules for both segments and a hybrid-mode outbound NAT rule that SNATs only lan-a→lan-b traffic to node1's opt2 address (192.168.20.1), leaving lan-b→lan-a traffic unmodified. Verified via tcpdump on node1's interfaces that node2→node3 traffic arrives at node3 sourced from 192.168.20.1, while node3→node2 traffic still arrives sourced from node3's real address (192.168.20.2). Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all three nodes: captured healthy baselines, restarted each node one at a time via native reboot, confirmed changed boot identity (boot_id for the RHEL nodes, kern.boottime for the FreeBSD/OPNsense router), and re-verified the asymmetric NAT behavior end-to-end after all three restarts.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (OPNsense/FreeBSD), node2 (RHEL9), node3 (RHEL9) topology and interfaces
Assigned static IPs to node2/node3 second NICs (enp8s0): 192.168.10.2/24 and 192.168.20.2/24, with static routes to reach the other lan via node1
Edited node1's /conf/config.xml to add opt1 (vtnet1, 192.168.10.1/24, lan-a) and opt2 (vtnet2, 192.168.20.1/24, lan-b) interfaces, backed up config.xml before each edit
Reconfigured interfaces via configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2
Added firewall pass rules for opt1 and opt2 (default-deny bypass) and reloaded filter
Verified baseline routing works and node3 sees node2's real source address prior to NAT
Added outbound NAT rule (hybrid mode) on node1: source 192.168.10.0/24 out interface opt2 -> target 192.168.20.1, reloaded filter
Verified via tcpdump on node1 vtnet1/vtnet2 that lan-a->lan-b traffic is SNATed to 192.168.20.1 while lan-b->lan-a traffic keeps original source
Captured pre-restart health baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, IP config, NAT rules) on all 3 nodes
Sequentially rebooted node2, then node3, then node1 (router last), polling each until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot identity on each node after restart
Re-verified interface/NAT config persistence and re-ran the asymmetric-NAT tcpdump test end-to-end after all restarts completed

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a (node2) and lan-b (node3)
evidence.summary: opt1/opt2 interfaces on node1 came up with correct IPs matching node2/node3 segments; node2 successfully pings across node1 to node3's lan-b address, proving routing works.

evidence.requirement: node2->node3 (lan-a to lan-b) traffic appears at node3 as originating from a chosen address on node1, not node2's own address
evidence.summary: Outbound NAT rule added (source 192.168.10.0/24 on opt2 -> target 192.168.20.1) and loaded into pf. tcpdump on node1's vtnet2 (lan-b wire) during a node2->node3 ping shows packets as '192.168.20.1 > 192.168.20.2', i.e. sourced from node1's opt2 address rather than node2's 192.168.10.2.

evidence.requirement: node3->node2 (lan-b to lan-a) traffic keeps its original source address (no NAT applied in that direction)
evidence.summary: tcpdump on node1's vtnet1 (lan-a wire) during a node3->node2 ping shows packets as '192.168.20.2 > 192.168.10.2', proving node3's real address is preserved when reaching node2 -- confirming the NAT rule only applies to the lan-a-to-lan-b direction.

evidence.requirement: Baseline behavior before NAT was added (falsification / control)
evidence.summary: Before the outbound NAT rule existed, tcpdump on node1's vtnet2 during node2->node3 ping showed the un-NATed flow as '192.168.10.2 > 192.168.20.2', proving the later SNAT behavior is caused by the added rule and not pre-existing routing behavior.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 9feeb0bb.../uptime pre-restart, issued native reboot, confirmed exec unreachable mid-restart, polled until boot_id changed to 6e496c6a... (proving a real restart), then confirmed enp8s0 static IP/routes and lan-b reachability recovered.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 31949c21.../uptime pre-restart, issued native reboot, confirmed exec unreachable mid-restart, polled until boot_id changed to 184a3590... (proving a real restart), then confirmed enp8s0 static IP/routes and lan-a reachability recovered.

evidence.requirement: node1 (OPNsense router) restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state including persisted NAT config
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime (17:28:39) pre-restart, issued native FreeBSD reboot, confirmed SSH/exec unreachable mid-restart, polled until kern.boottime changed to 17:34:29 (proving a real restart), then confirmed opt1/opt2 interfaces and the outbound NAT rule persisted from config.xml after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Full asymmetric NAT behavior re-verified end-to-end after all three node restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart, repeated the tcpdump verification: node2->node3 traffic on vtnet2 still shows source 192.168.20.1 (SNAT active), and node3->node2 traffic on vtnet1 still shows source 192.168.20.2 (no NAT), confirming the configuration and its asymmetric behavior survived all three node restarts.
